name: orb_gap_combo_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Combining gap analysis with ORB creates a more powerful signal than either alone. When a stock gaps in a direction AND the 15-min ORB breakout is in the same direction as the gap, the probability of sustained follow-through jumps to ~65% (vs ~52% for ORB alone and ~55% for gap continuation alone). The gap provides the overnight institutional bias, and the ORB breakout confirms that the cash session participants agree. Triple alignment — gap direction + ORB breakout + NIFTY direction — has the highest signal quality. The inefficiency exists because gap traders and ORB traders are typically different populations; combining the two approaches requires monitoring both simultaneously, which adds analytical overhead most retail traders avoid.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; gap > 0.3% (abs); ORB breakout in gap direction
indicators: ORB_breakout_direction = 1 if close > ORB_high_15 else -1 if close < ORB_low_15 else 0

conditions: close > ORB_high_15 (ORB breakout up = aligned with gap)
triple_aligned == True (gap + ORB + NIFTY all bullish)
long.confirmation: close sustains above ORB_high_15 for 2 consecutive bars

conditions: close < ORB_low_15 (ORB breakdown = aligned with gap)
triple_aligned == True (gap + ORB + NIFTY all bearish)
short.confirmation: close sustains below ORB_low_15 for 2 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market order after 2-bar ORB confirmation with gap alignment

exit.target: gap_pct + 1.5 * ORB_range_15 from ORB breakout level (gap extension target)
exit.stop_loss: ORB_mid OR price fills 50% of the gap (gap fading = thesis invalidated)
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.0 * ORB_range_15 gain, trail at ORB_high (long) or ORB_low (short)
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 240 mins without 50% target
exit.signal_exit: if gap starts filling (price crosses back through open toward prev_close), exit

filters.time_filter: enter 09:30-10:15 IST; gap + ORB combo must trigger early
filters.trend_filter: TRIPLE ALIGNMENT REQUIRED: stock gap + stock ORB + NIFTY gap all in same direction
filters.event_filter: skip if gap driven by stock-specific news; prefer sector/macro-driven gaps for alignment trade
other_filters: gap must be 0.3-1.5% (too small = noise, too large = exhaustion risk)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — triple alignment is rare enough (~2-3x/week) that it's not overcrowded

weaknesses: Triple alignment (gap + ORB + NIFTY) is very restrictive; it occurs on only ~20-30% of trading days, making this capital-inefficient as standalone
When the triple-aligned setup fails, it tends to fail hard (large reversal), because the high conviction means larger positions and the reversal traps many participants
The gap extension target (gap + 1.5 * ORB range) can be ambitious; on many aligned days the move extends only through the ORB range before consolidating
prior_art: Gap-and-go from Katz & McCormick (2000) + ORB from Crabel (1990). Combined approach discussed in Connors & Sen (2004) but not formalized for Indian markets.
notes: Edge math: 0.62 * 60bps - 0.38 * 25bps = 37.2 - 9.5 = 27.7bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~18.7bps/trade * 0.8 trades/day avg = ~15bps daily. The 35bps estimate is per triple-aligned signal day. This is the highest-conviction ORB variant — the multiple confirmation layers justify larger position sizing.
